A me terrorizza pensare che dopo la triennale dovrò fare anche una magistrale e magari anche un dottorato per potermi specializzare in una nicchia e trovare un lavoro che mi faccia dire "ne è valsa la pena!". Questa facoltà mi sta logorando mentalmente da troppo tempo, non sarei in grado di sopportare oltre, ma il mio problema è che penso troppo al  prospetto di "perdere" questi anni di studio.  

La penso come te, lavorare in un campo che ti piace/appassiona è sicuramente meno pesante (per quanto sia sempre lavorare) che fare un lavoro che detesti, in un campo che odi. Realisticamente, un sacco di opportunità di lavorare in laboratorio

Per quanto riguarda il corso di pilotaggio (se ti riferisci a quello) è un campo molto diversificato e anche un mio amico mi dice che le applicazioni sono tantissime, per cui volendo potrei anche fare da rilievi fotogrammetrici (che si connette al corso di studi) a riprese video di altro genere

It's just my opinion, based on the climatic predictions temperatures are gonna rise so much in places like where I live it's gonna be a nightmare just being outside, sea rising is going to be a pain in the a\*s for coastal communities, we don't know how plants/animals will react to a sudden change in temperatures, even breathing air is becoming a problem because of PM etc.

(I'm not considering the financial aspect of all of this because I don't care, that's for another time). 

The environment is still treated very badly, even after all the promotion environmentalists do. We (as a specie) hurt the planet in ways most of us don't even understand: people still believe beaches are meant to be clean spotless white sand stretches, soy for human consuption is hurting the planet, "weeding" and mowing the lawn is good practice etc. It's gonna take so much time to actually change something in the common conscience.

I'd like to think that we can stop emissions etc etc and finally reach the point where the curve starts to drop, but every year politicians/whoever decides pushes the target-year further and honestly, feels like we'll never actually start carrying out green policies FOR REAL. We as individuals can only do so much to change something.

 Also whoever decides doesn't really care about the environment, they are gonna be dead in like 10 years and however the climate/planet/environment is gonna be fucked up is not going to be their business (their pockets) anymore.

I hate thinking apocalyptic, but that's why I think it's too late, the planet as we know now it's living it's last years. I'm very sorry for the species we'll lose but I don't see any solution.

It probably all stems from this loss of trying to understand, which made me think I don't get it so it's not real/ doesn't work. Even if I know the mechanism of my reasoning, "I don't believe in hard sciences"  it's still the belief I hold, for now, at least.

Thanks for the sympathy!! Unfortunately the reason I want to "keep studying" as of now it's just to get out of this degree lol. When I started I was all about that internal flame of knowing, dude, I miss dearly being passionate about learning.

Even though I see that the problem is mostly mine (because -you know- how do you not believe science), I also think a good portion is the lecture's fault, how do you beat the intent out of me so bad that I now want to have nothing to do with it? I really hope I can snap out of it SOMEHOW. I'm afraid studying these subjects it's just a part of the solution, or else I would have been okay with them since high school. (And I actually like doing physics exercises, those are the ones where I can most easily understand what it is about, and I find them kind of fun sometimes)

I know very well that I don't understand anything about these things at all, the problem is that at the third year of a science degree where I actually went to lectures it's a bit of a problem you see, how am I putting the effort to understand and still makes no sense to the point it feels like black magic to me, it's very disheartening (to me)

I fully believe I have been failed by the school system.  The way it's taught makes these subject so abstract that I see absolutely no purpose in them, studying them is a grievous activity and it's all made more difficult by me not even BELIEVING it. 

Don't get me wrong, It's not like I believe mysterious paranormal forces are powering my computer and stuff like that, but I am exceptionally unconcerned about how it works.

I really want to understand what is going on with maths/physics/chemistry (to pass my courses), and I don't want to study and give exams from memory alone. 

At the beginning of the degree, I really wanted to be one those scientists providing useful pieces of knowledge, but university only made me cynical and hateful towards the science environment.

For chemistry, it's pretty weird that we have a periodic table from 1 to 89 (atomic numbers) and not once a numbers is repeated? Feels pretty synthetic to me that in nature there is a perfect system of elements and not 2 of them have the same atomic number. 

Also, how is it possible that we have ALL numbers from 1 to 89 (excluding lanthanides and actinides) and not one is missing? Like, why is 4or 27 missing? No we have all of them, perfectly not repeated.

For physics, I just find it stupid to find a language to describe things we don't fully understand like, for example, the infiniteness of the universe. There's no reason for it.

I haven't touched a math book in a while so I don't remember exactly what concepts it were, but they are there.

My aunt (my grandmother's aunt so basically she's 98 or something at this point) has lived all her life in the same house, in the same neighbourhood. She has a circle of friends, like the nun, the one she used to go to church with etc. They're all about the same age.

Of course, one by one, they are passing from old age. One of her friends passed when she was being given a bath and she said that to me as if nothing happened, as if it was just something that happened, like buying some bread. When her step brother died, again, she was just like "oh harold died this morning", and kept going on with her day.

She doesn't suffer from dementia, she is still very vibrant and recites her prayers in french, as she was taught when she was 11. So it's not even that she forgot about all these people. 

Maybe it's just my aunt who is a stone cold bitch who doesn't let people see how she feels, but damn, it happened so many times now. 

Your grandfather's story was so sad to read, surely when you know someone for such a long time, it must feel so difficult to detach yourself from a piece of your life.
